title: API onboarding project profile
description: Everything the dynamic API generation solution needs to know about ONE project. Each field here corresponds to a place where the PAM implementation currently hardcodes a PAM fact. A profile that validates clean is a project the harness can run against without a code change. x-blocker fields must be answered before any execution; x-degrades fields reduce coverage when absent but do not stop a run.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the profile was authored against.

project.description: Who and what. Used for report headers, evidence paths and ticket references.

key.description: Short uppercase code, e.g. PAM, IDEV. Used in filenames.

name.description: Human name of the product under test.

owner.description: The person who answers questions about it. A profile with no named owner has no route to resolving an UNKNOWN.

tracker.description: Jira (or other) project key for raising defects, e.g. PROJ.

workspace.description: Where things live on disk. Replaces a harness's hardcoded REPO / ROOT resolution.

root_markers.description: Directory names that identify the workspace root by search rather than a fixed number of parent hops, so scripts keep working when moved. PAM uses ['Reports', 'Automation gitlab repo'].

reference_repo.description: Relative path to a repo read as a GENERATION INPUT only. Never executed, never written to.

reports_dir.description: Relative path where dated run folders are written.

flows_dir.description: Relative path holding flow JSON, hand-written and generated.

environment.description: The target environment. One profile addresses exactly one environment; copy the profile for another.

name.description: Environment identifier, e.g. QA or STAGING.

api_base.description: Scheme, host and port serving the API. Often NOT the same port as the app.

app_base.description: The UI/app origin, when it differs. PAM: API :6302, app :1302 — confusing the two produces 404s that read as missing endpoints.

is_production.description: MUST be false. A true value is a hard refusal, not a warning.

config_format.description: How environment settings are stored, so the loader knows how to parse them.

config_file.description: Relative path to that file. Assume its contents are secret even if the repo tracks them in plaintext (PAM's 20 env files do).

verify_tls.description: false only for a QA host with a self-signed certificate. Record WHY in notes.

stability.description: Measured, not assumed. PAM QA: poor — 17 downtime pauses costing 85 of 329 minutes in one run.

auth.description: How a request is authenticated, and the lockout policy that governs how often credentials may be presented.

kind.description: Nothing can execute until this is known and proven with one successful call.

token_endpoint.description: Path or absolute URL that issues a token. PAM: /arcontoken.

credential_keys.description: Maps a logical credential to the KEY NAME in config_file. Never put a secret value in a profile.

extra_headers.description: Static headers every request needs, e.g. an API version header.

env_var_override.description: Env var that supplies a token directly and bypasses the credential endpoint entirely. The safest option for an unattended run.

cache_file.description: Where the single per-run token is cached.

lockout_risk.description: high = the account locks after N failures and the account is shared with something that matters. PAM is high: repeated /arcontoken calls locked GenericScheduler, which is also the data-warehouse ETL account.

max_token_attempts_per_run.description: 1 whenever lockout_risk is high. Retry-on-failure and account lockout are fundamentally incompatible.

latch_on_failure.description: A failed attempt blocks all later attempts, in this run AND future runs, until a human clears it. Without this, 'once per run' silently becomes 'every run' — which is how PAM's account was locked.

roles.description: Distinct identities needed to exercise authorization boundaries. Absent this, every authorization test is inert.

invalid_token_sample.description: A deliberately invalid credential, for negative auth tests. Sending a VALID token while asserting 401 makes the assertion unfalsifiable — 1,153 PAM cases did exactly that.

catalogue.description: Where the machine-readable list of endpoints comes from. Without this there is nothing to generate from.

adapter.description: openapi is the cheapest path by a wide margin. java-constants is what PAM needed because no spec exists.

source.description: Path or URL the adapter reads.

expected_count.description: Endpoint count the adapter should yield. A drift here means the catalogue moved — fail loudly rather than silently covering less.

count_basis.description: WHAT was counted. PAM's file yields 1,336 / 1,321 / 1,308 / 1,306 depending on basis; the canonical figure is 1,306 distinct (controller, action) pairs. Quote a figure with its basis, never bare.

allow_verbs.description: Verbs the executor may issue. PAM: GET, POST — which is 99.7% of its surface.

verb_distribution.description: Measured, per verb. Reveals whether verb-based safety guards can work at all.

templated_marker.description: How the catalogue expresses a path parameter, e.g. '{id}'. Templated paths cannot be called without a value.

exclude_patterns.description: Endpoints to drop at generation time for reasons other than safety, e.g. an undeployed surface.

payloads.description: Where request bodies come from. Absent, coverage degrades to read-only: creates cannot be generated.

coverage.description: Measured create coverage. Budget for THIS, not for tooling — it was the largest single cost on PAM.

binding_confidence.description: How a body was bound to an endpoint. PAM's documentation binds by page proximity, so some bindings are simply wrong.

unique_fields.description: Fields that must be randomised per run or the second run returns 'already exists' instead of creating.

envelope.description: How the API signals success and failure. The single most consequential section: get it wrong and every assertion is decorative.

status_is_authoritative.description: true only if a rejected request reliably returns 4xx. PAM: false — 1,022 cases returned HTTP 200 while failing validation. MEASURE it; do not accept a developer's assurance.

shapes_measured.description: How many distinct top-level response shapes were observed in a probe. 0 means no probe has been run, which means the assertions are guesses. PAM: 31.

shape_census.description: Path to the probe output listing every shape with an example endpoint.

success_fields.description: Candidate names for the boolean success flag, ALL casings that occur. PAM ships PascalCase 'Success' 1,580 times and camelCase 'success' 0 times — a case-sensitive parser looking for the latter fails on every response the API can produce.

result_containers.description: Field names holding the payload rows, e.g. Result, aaData, Data, items.

created_messages.description: Message substrings that mean a write really happened.

noop_messages.description: Message substrings that mean nothing was written DESPITE a success flag. PAM returns Success:true with 'Already Exists'.

error_code_registry.description: Path to the known error codes, or 'NOT DOCUMENTED'. Match on prefix and record an unrecognised code as an observation — a hardcoded allowlist turns an undocumented product code into a failed test.

non_json_expected.description: true if some endpoints answer with a bare array, bare boolean, empty string or HTML. PAM: 127 of 1,868 responses were not JSON objects at all.

identity_prelude.description: The hops that discover the context ids every later payload needs. THE MOST COMMONLY MISSED INPUT. Without it every payload is environment-bound and the flows are not portable. PAM discovers LOB then server group then user group.

find_extract.description: Filtered row join — select the row WHERE a field equals a carried value, then take ids from it. Blind Result[0] chaining silently picks the wrong record.

id_aliases.description: Maps a payload field name (lowercased) to the prelude variable that supplies it, so a generator can substitute discovered ids into literal bodies. PAM maps lobid/lob_id/lobsid all to ${LOB_ID}.

safety.description: Deny-by-default controls. Non-negotiable whenever the harness can write.

default_mode.description: MUST be plan-only. A bare run issues zero HTTP calls; an explicit flag is required to make any.

blocklist.description: Action-name substring -> reason. Enforced at PLANNING time, before a request is built. PAM's three entries stop the IIS application pool; three sequential calls took the whole API to 503 with no recovery.

destructive_name_regex.description: Names that must not be called unless teardown is explicitly permitted. GUARD ON NAMES, NOT VERBS: PAM expresses deletion as POST /api/X/DeleteThing, so a destructive call looks like an ordinary POST.

teardown.description: created-only means the harness may delete records it created in this run and nothing else.

health_probe.description: A cheap, safe, read-only call used to decide whether the environment is up. Must not be blocklisted and must not write.

breaker_consecutive_5xx.description: Consecutive server errors or timeouts before the run pauses.

downtime_wait_s.description: Wait, probe, then RESUME from the paused hop — never restart.

body_cap_bytes.description: Cap response bodies. One PAM endpoint returns 1.1 MB with no filter parameter.

redact_keys.description: Substrings whose values are redacted before anything reaches disk.

rate_limit.description: Documented limits, if the API publishes them. Replaces a fixed throttle with limit-aware backoff.

validation.description: Which assertion layers apply. Keep every layer that the API's own behaviour makes meaningful.

layers.description: Subset of L1 http-status, L2 content-type, L3 envelope, L4 message-semantics, L5 chain-key-extracted, L6 record-exists, L7 latency, L8 schema, L9 mandatory-fields, L10 business-rule, L11 db-persistence, L12 security. Drop L3/L4 ONLY if status_is_authoritative is true.

sla_ms.description: Per-operation-class latency budgets. One global budget tuned on reads produces false failures on every write; PAM writes take 5-7 s.

database.description: L11 only. Read-only least-privilege account, or omit the layer.

reporting.description: Where evidence goes and how long it lives.

run_dir_pattern.description: e.g. 'artifacts/runs/{stamp}' with {stamp} as YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS. A dated folder per execution is what makes N-1 vs N possible at all.

retention.description: forever is strongly preferred. Auto-deleting prior output destroys comparability, and you only discover that when you need a baseline.

evidence_per_call.description: One redacted request/response/verdict file per call. This is what lets a reviewer verify a single claim, and what makes offline re-scoring possible.

workbook.description: Emit an .xlsx alongside the markdown. Requires openpyxl — the only third-party dependency in the whole solution.

benchmark_baseline.description: Run folder that is N-1. A metric absent from N-1 is reported as N/A, never dropped.

unknowns.description: Every fact not yet established, each naming what would settle it and who owns the answer. An empty list on a new project is a warning sign, not an achievement — it usually means nobody looked.

settled_by.description: The specific artifact, call or person that answers it.

blocks.description: true if execution cannot start until answered.

provenance.description: How this profile came to say what it says.

probe_run.description: The run folder whose probe established the envelope section.

measured_run.description: The run folder the measured counts come from.
